cardiac_arrest.name: Cardiac Arrest
cardiac_arrest.subtitle: Not breathing — CPR required immediately

steps.title: Shout for Help NOW
steps.description: Point at a specific person: 'YOU — in the blue shirt — call 108 immediately!' This prevents the bystander effect where everyone assumes someone else will help.

steps.title: Confirm — No Breathing
steps.description: Look at the chest (rising?), listen near the mouth, feel for breath on your cheek. Do this for no more than 10 seconds.

steps.title: Position Your Hands
steps.description: Kneel beside them. Place the heel of one hand on the CENTER of their chest (on the breastbone). Place your other hand on top and interlace your fingers.

steps.title: Compress HARD and FAST
steps.description: Push the chest down at least 5 cm (2 inches). Release fully between compressions. Rate: 100–120 per minute. Think of 'Stayin' Alive' by Bee Gees.

steps.title: Do Not Stop
steps.description: Continue CPR until: the ambulance arrives, the person starts breathing normally, or you are too exhausted to continue. If another person is present, swap every 2 minutes.

doNot: Do NOT stop CPR until ambulance personnel take over
Do NOT give food or water at any time
Do NOT leave them alone even for a moment
Do NOT panic — CPR does not need to be perfect to save a life

head_trauma.name: Head Trauma
head_trauma.subtitle: Unconscious but breathing

steps.title: WARNING — Do NOT Move Them
steps.description: A head trauma victim may also have a spinal injury. Moving the neck can cause permanent paralysis. Keep them exactly where they are.

steps.title: Protect the Airway
steps.description: If unconscious but breathing, ONLY IF no spinal risk suspected: gently roll them to their side (recovery position) to prevent choking on vomit. Support the head throughout.

steps.title: Control Head Bleeding
steps.description: Press a clean cloth gently over any head wound. Apply steady, gentle pressure. Do NOT press directly on the skull if it feels uneven or sunken.

steps.title: Monitor Breathing Every 30 Seconds
steps.description: Watch the chest rise. Count their breaths. Normal is 12–20 per minute. If breathing becomes irregular or stops, begin CPR immediately.

doNot: Do NOT remove a helmet — this risks further injury
Do NOT give anything to eat or drink
Do NOT shake or slap them to wake them up
Do NOT put anything in their mouth

fracture.name: Fracture or Severe Bleeding
fracture.subtitle: Broken bone or significant blood loss

steps.title: Stop the Bleeding First
steps.description: Apply firm, direct pressure with the cleanest material available — a shirt, dupatta, anything. Press hard and continuously. Do NOT lift the cloth to check; apply more material on top if needed.

steps.title: Support — Do Not Straighten
steps.description: Support the injured limb in the exact position you found it using your hands or folded clothing. A broken bone that is bent should STAY bent until paramedics arrive.

steps.title: Raise the Limb If Possible
steps.description: Gently elevate the injured arm or leg above the level of the heart. This reduces blood flow to the area and slows blood loss significantly.

steps.title: Prevent Shock
steps.description: Lay them down flat if possible. Cover with a blanket or coat to maintain body temperature. Talk to them calmly and reassure them constantly.

doNot: Do NOT attempt to push a bone back into place
Do NOT remove any object that is embedded in a wound
Do NOT apply a tight tourniquet unless bleeding cannot be stopped otherwise
Do NOT offer food or water

burns.name: Burns
burns.subtitle: Heat, chemical, or friction burns

steps.title: Cool the Burn — Full 20 Minutes
steps.description: Pour cool (not cold, not iced) running water continuously over the burned area for a full 20 minutes. Use a water bottle, tap, stream — any clean water source. Timing is critical.

steps.title: Remove Clothing and Jewelry
steps.description: Carefully and gently remove clothing, rings, watches, and other items near the burn. Do this ONLY if they are not stuck to the skin. If stuck, leave them and tell the paramedics.

steps.title: Cover the Burn Loosely
steps.description: After the 20-minute cooling, cover the burned area with clean cling film laid flat (not wrapped), or a clean plastic bag. If unavailable, a clean non-fluffy cloth works.

steps.title: Prevent Shock and Hypothermia
steps.description: Cover the REST of the body (not the burn) with a blanket. Cooling the burn while keeping the body warm is critical — burns cause rapid heat loss.

doNot: Do NOT use ice — it causes further tissue damage
Do NOT apply butter, oil, toothpaste, or any cream
Do NOT burst blisters that form
Do NOT use fluffy cotton wool directly on the burn
Do NOT wrap cling film around a limb — lay it flat only

spinal.name: Spinal Injury
spinal.subtitle: Neck or back injury — extreme caution required

steps.title: STOP — Absolute No Movement
steps.description: Do NOT move the person under any circumstances. A misaligned spine can sever the spinal cord — permanent paralysis can result from even a small movement. This is the most important instruction.

steps.title: Stabilize the Head
steps.description: Kneel directly behind their head. Place both hands firmly on either side of the skull (not the neck). Hold their head in the position you found it. Do not try to straighten it.

steps.title: Keep Them Calm and Still
steps.description: Talk to them calmly and clearly: 'You are safe. Help is coming. It is very important that you stay completely still. Do not try to move.'

steps.title: Monitor Breathing Continuously
steps.description: Watch their chest and listen for breathing every 30 seconds. If they stop breathing, CPR becomes the priority — you must begin compressions even with a spinal injury.

doNot: Do NOT move the head, neck, or spine for any reason
Do NOT try to straighten or reposition the body
Do NOT remove a helmet — this is a spinal precaution
Do NOT give food or water
Do NOT leave them to go get help — send someone else
